doc.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023

title: Two drummers in Stuff: ego and playing double drums
summary: Playing with Steve Gadd required no discussion; Parker cites his brothers' drum sets and earlier double-drum work with Rick Marotta and Jeff Porcaro.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: How much does it have to do with your personal ego?

I mean I was going to get to Stuff later which we could do but being cognizant of what a percussionist is doing certainly applies in this situation, when you have two drummers going. And I doubt that you had discussions about who’s going to do what.

Yep. That was part of the — it sounds cliché, but part of the magic of the group was that Steve and I never discussed, you know I’ll play cross stick and you go to the bell and then I’ll play sixteenths on the hi-hat and you do bass drum. We never discussed a single element. We just sat down and played together. The fact that I grew up with three younger brothers and my dad playing drums in the house, often there were five sets of drums set up, made it feel pretty natural to play with another drummer. And I had done recordings, there’s a Sandborn record with me and Rick Marotta playing drums, double drums, and I did a tour with Boz Scaggs with Jeff Porcaro for the first month of the tour we were playing double drums with Jeff Porcaro so the thing with Steve was great. We just hit it off personally and hit it off musically. You know, and it was part of the attraction of the group that two drummers but it wasn’t super loud and it wasn’t — we weren’t stepping all over each other.
